name: Rock Health on AI in Healthcare: Funding, Adoption and Regulation
title: Rock Health on AI in Healthcare: Funding, Adoption and Regulation
answer: Rock Health is a digital health venture research organisation whose site publishes survey findings, funding analyses and regulatory commentary on AI in healthcare. Its most useful single contribution is the 2025 Consumer Adoption of Digital Health Survey, which found that 32% of U.S. adults have turned to AI chatbots for health information, double the 16% a year earlier, with nearly three-quarters of those users choosing ChatGPT.

sections.body: Rock Health publishes research, survey findings and commentary on digital health, drawing on its own venture funding database and on surveys it runs with partners such as the American Academy of Family Physicians and Evidation. The pages read span consumer and clinician surveys, analyses of FDA-cleared AI devices, funding breakdowns by use case, guidance for pharma, and announcements of a primary care initiative. Dates stated across the pages run from a 2018 FDA working group through a survey fielded in December 2025, so the material is a mix of current findings and older reference analyses rather than a single dated report.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The consumer survey, fielded in December 2025 with 8,000 U.S. Census-matched adults, found that 32% had ever used AI chatbots for health information, double the 16% of a year earlier, and that 64% of those users engage weekly or more often. Nearly three-quarters of AI users turned to ChatGPT, equal to 23% of all respondents, while provider-offered and payer-offered chatbots were used by 5% and 4% respectively. Top queries were treatment options after a diagnosis, a diagnosis from symptoms, and prescription drug information. A companion survey of more than 1,200 primary care clinicians, run with the American Academy of Family Physicians between September and November 2024, found that half had used AI tools for at least one work use case, most commonly clerical support, and that 65% had limited or no input on AI purchasing decisions. Rock Health's funding work reports that since 2023 more than 280 venture-backed U.S. digital health startups with AI-enabled solutions raised $6.3 billion, 34% of all sector funding, with two-thirds building for provider organisations. An analysis of the FDA's device list counted 343 AI- and ML-enabled entries from 1997 through June 2021, 70% in radiology. A 2018 working group with Evidation examined regulatory questions around ground truth data, and a pharma article sets out a two-phase method for constructing AI use cases around actions such as sort, match, score, enhance, create and chat.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source gives 32% of U.S. adults having used AI chatbots for health information, up from 16%; 64% of users engaging weekly or more; 23% of all respondents using ChatGPT; 5% and 4% using provider and payer chatbots; 8,000 survey respondents; 1,200-plus clinicians surveyed; 50% of clinicians using AI at work and 65% with limited or no purchasing input; $6.3 billion raised by more than 280 AI-enabled startups since 2023, 34% of sector funding and 67% aimed at providers; 343 FDA entries through June 2021 with 70% radiology and 12% cardiovascular; and 130-plus U.S. startups selling AI tools for pharma.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in healthcare gets two things here that are hard to find together: measured adoption data from large, methodologically described surveys of both consumers and primary care clinicians, and a running record of where venture capital is going within clinical AI. The consumer numbers show demand arriving through general-purpose chatbots rather than through health system tools, which reframes where patients first encounter AI. The clinician survey shows adoption concentrated in clerical work and a workforce largely excluded from purchasing decisions. The funding and FDA analyses give a sense of which use cases and device categories have attracted money and regulatory clearance.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Healthcare

sections.body: The material is a collection of separate pages of varying age, from a 2018 regulatory working group to a survey fielded in December 2025, so figures are not directly comparable across pages. Several analyses, including the FDA device list and the AI/ML funding breakdown, stop in 2021 and do not reflect later clearances or investment. Rock Health is a venture firm, and its funding figures come from its own database, so the framing of opportunity is oriented toward investors and startups. The clinician survey covers primary care only, and the pharma guidance is aimed at industry decision makers rather than clinicians or patients.
